# Summary of Garry Kasparov
Garry Kasparov, born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Soviet Union, is a former world chess champion and political activist. Of Jewish and Armenian descent, he adopted his mother's surname at age 12 and fled anti-Armenian pogroms in 1990. Kasparov began serious chess training at age seven under Vladimir Makogonov and quickly rose through the ranks, becoming the youngest-ever world No. 1 at 21 in 1984. He won the World Chess Championship in 1985 after a contentious match with Anatoly Karpov and defended his title in several subsequent matches. After a break with FIDE in 1993, Kasparov established the Professional Chess Association and caused a split in the world championship title. He lost his classical world title to Vladimir Kramnik in 2000 but remained the top-rated player until retiring from regular competition in 2005. Post-retirement, Kasparov remained active in chess through exhibitions, coaching, and launching his online chess platform.
Kasparov is also a prominent political figure and outspoken critic of Vladimir Putin's administration. Initially a Communist Party member, he left the party in 1990 and subsequently engaged in pro-democracy activism in Russia, leading movements like the United Civil Front and The Other Russia coalition. He ran briefly for Russian presidency in 2008 but withdrew due to government obstruction. Facing repeated harassment and fearing persecution, Kasparov fled Russia in 2013 and continues his opposition from exile, advocating for democratic reforms and criticizing Putin’s policies on various international issues. He holds Croatian citizenship and resides in New York City. Beyond chess and politics, Kasparov has authored numerous books on chess history, strategy, and political commentary, including *Winter Is Coming* , which critiques Putin and calls for coordinated democratic action.
